input: I’m using a layered 3D-style reprojection rather than a simple pan. The road gets depth from its vanishing point, the buildings get nearer toward the frame edges, and the dog/shadow are separated and re-anchored at the same ground point. That should make the background rotate around the stationary subject instead of making the whole photograph slide uniformly.

The check caught two artifacts worth fixing before handoff: a stretched road strip at the newly exposed left edge, and a crescent of copied asphalt attached to the dog’s shadow. I’m extending the source with reflected street texture for the orbit’s newly revealed border, separating the dog from its shadow, and rendering the shadow independently at the planted paws. I’m also tightening the arc slightly so the motion stays photographic.
